Set the Row Context Menu's target field for the Name Manipulation Inherit actions to this field's internal name.

The game doesn't read this param. It is an input of the map pattern lottery FromSoftware ran before release, whose results ship as LotResultSmallBaseAndSpot, LotResultMapPatternFlag and LotResultPlayArea. Edit those to change the map patterns.

Many fields of this param are inputs of the map pattern lottery FromSoftware ran before release, and the game doesn't read them (their descriptions say which). Changing them has no effect unless the LotResult params are changed to match.
Double-click to show or hide this section.
Which of the 100 random slots this row has set, the row that holds the other slots, and the map objects that use it.
{0} of {1} slots set: map objects on this row are placed in {2}% of sessions.
Each session draws one slot from 0 to 99. A map object whose Random Appear Param ID is this row is placed only if the drawn slot is set here. Map objects on the same row always appear together.
Set every slot: placed in every session.
Swap set and clear slots, so this row places in exactly the sessions it didn't.
{0} rows have ID {1}. The game uses the first of them.
This row has exactly the slots this one doesn't. Of two map objects on these rows, exactly one appears in each session. Click to go to it.
No row has exactly the other slots.
The ID of the row Make Complement Row creates. Retail pairs use neighbouring IDs, such as 100 and 101.
Add a row with exactly the slots this one doesn't, so two map objects on the two rows never appear together and one of them always does.
A row with ID {0} already exists. Pick a free ID.
The map objects whose Random Appear Param ID is this row, in every map of the project. Loaded maps are read as they are in the Map Editor, the rest from the project's files.
Read every map of the project to find which map objects use which rows. The result isn't updated as you edit maps: rescan after changing them.
No map object uses this row.
{0}. Click to show it in the Map Editor.
Where this row puts something in the maps: the attach point and the small base placed on it, or the map objects this row changes.
SmallBaseAndSpotAttachPoint has no row {0}, so this site has no place in the map.
No SmallBaseAttach region has this entity ID in {0}. The row's Placement Location and Rotation are measured in the small tile.
No region has entity ID {0} in the tile {1} or the larger tiles covering it.
The project has none of the maps this attach point can be in: the small tile {0} or the larger tiles covering it.

Find the SmallBaseAttach region the small base is placed at, then load its map in the Map Editor and select it. It is searched for in {0}, in that order: most regions are in the large tile that covers the small tile the row names.
Find the attach region, then load its tile and the small base in the Map Editor and show the base at the region, with the Session Preview at variation {0}. Only the view changes: nothing is saved.
Load the small base in the Map Editor with the Session Preview showing variation {0}: the map objects a session with this lot result places.
Assets and enemies in the small base this variation places, besides those with no Variation. From the map scan at {0}: rescan after editing the map.
Read every map of the project, to check that the small base has map objects at this variation.
Matches map objects with Scenario Placement keys {0}, {1}, {2}

A map object's Scenario Placement Key 1, Key 2 and Step are compared with this row's place scenario, condition scenario and condition stage. For an enemy, the matching row's Chara Init Param ID is used.
The map objects whose Scenario Placement keys match this row, in every map of the project.
